review: Advanced unarmed techniques, unusual melee equipment and firearm failure procedures inventoried. Numeric rows transcribed; weapon/trait catalogues, source table visual audit and follow-on cover rules remain pending.

entries.acceptance: Two free hands and a qualifying unarmed parry permit next-turn arm capture within one yard: enter close range and attack with the applicable grappling skill, allowing normal defense. Offensive entry instead follows a successful grapple that survived the target’s escape opportunity.
Holder gains +4 in escape contest; each failed escape gives victim a cumulative -1 on later escape attempts. Store penalty on this lock episode, not permanently on the character.

On turns after capture, compare best eligible grappling skill/strength with victim’s higher strength/health. Victory margin gives crushing damage through rigid and eligible natural armor, ignoring flexible armor and the skin-limited natural layer. This passive contest does not consume an attack.

Crippling the held arm drops its item and ends further limb damage from the lock. Later successful contests still cause corresponding shock/stun. Holder can also make close attacks with victim defense -4 plus other actual penalties; do not invent extra usable hands.
Rear two-handed hold uses throwing-grapple skill at -2 or wrestling at -3, with normal rear defense rules for an aware victim. Capture head/neck, not arms/legs; escape contest gives holder +5.

Starting on holder’s next turn, victim loses one fatigue each holder turn until escape. Optional simultaneous crushing uses the ordinary strangling contest at holder strength +3; prevent duplicate fatigue from the same restraint.
Rear close-range elbow uses brawling or trained striking skill at -2 with no facing penalty; selected location adds another -1. Damage is ordinary punch. Forward elbow uses normal punch rules.
Close-only knee uses brawling or trained striking skill at -1 and ordinary kick damage. Held victim defends at -2; a front grapple permits groin targeting without its ordinary location penalty.

Trained hand/foot strike can take an additional -2 attack and -1 damage to convert crushing to piercing. It can then target eyes/vitals, but self-injury applies against armor at least one rather than three.

Two-handed neck/limb grapple must survive an escape opportunity before strength-4 versus higher victim strength/health contest. Victory causes swing crushing to held location through rigid and eligible natural armor, bypassing flexible/skin-limited layers. Later turns allow repeated attempts with ordinary victim actions.

Trample requires size advantage at least two, or one against prone victim when attacker is not prone. Attack best dexterity/brawling, dodge only; damage thrust crushing with hoof bonus one per die. Size advantage at least three uses large-area injury.

After knocking victim down by collision and continuing movement, automatically trample without attack/defense rolls using half attacker strength rounded down. Distinguish this subsequent damage from the collision itself.
Cloak distraction uses feint; cloak grapple uses cloak skill at close/one-yard reach and ordinary restraint rules. Track cloak occupancy and loss of defensive availability.

Author maps an object to a suitable weapon profile with actual dimensions/material. Clumsy objects can take -1 through -3 attack/parry or higher strength requirement; undersized/light/dull objects can reduce damage. Record chosen changes before action rather than accepting arbitrary damage afterward.
Fencing parry gains retreat +3 and half ordinary repeated-parry penalty, but subtracts encumbrance level and cannot parry flails. Apply once with shared defense logic.
Flail attacks penalize parry -4 and block -2; fencing weapons cannot parry them. Do not convert prohibition into a large numeric penalty.

Rear cord restraint requires unaware or helpless target, skill attack at neck -5. Specific defense permits hand/ready close weapon parry at -3, with mental-stun penalties if applicable; reconcile this exception with ordinary unawareness defense denial.
Successful interposed hand takes no damage from rope but wire can injure it. Resolve actual material and captured body part instead of applying neck injury despite successful defense.

From attack turn onward, holder may strangle with strength +3; rope uses crushing with neck factor 1.5, wire cutting with neck factor two, and suffocation begins. Victim escape compares best strength-5 or eligible grappling skill-3 against holder’s cord skill.
Improvised cord gives -2 skill. Unhandled wire inflicts own thrust cutting to each user hand; protect actual hands and avoid one shared-location injury entry.

Swing-impaling weapon causing penetrating injury becomes embedded. On following turn holder may release freely or spend ready plus strength check to extract; failure leaves it unusable and prevents moving while holding it. Critical failure prevents ordinary in-combat extraction.

Successful extraction adds half the original wound as new injury; failed attempts cause none. Resolve half rounding explicitly and preserve original wound identity. A weapon needing post-use readying still requires another turn afterward.

Victim departure while weapon is held compares strength: victim win pulls weapon from holder, holder win prevents movement, tie extracts with extra injury. Keep item attachment and holder grip separate.
Shield bash can target front or shield side using actual attack profile. Shield collision is unavailable with a buckler even though ordinary shield bash may be allowed.
Whip disarm gets +2 contest. Target entanglement instead takes extra -4, no immediate damage, and uses lariat restraint procedures. Both require a valid declared attack mode.

Whips take -2 parry and cannot attack/parry same turn; long whips become unready after either. Two-yard whip readies in one turn, length at least three in two turns. Preserve active length and weapon definition.
Ordinary whip crack takes -4 skill for +2 damage. Arm/hand wound requires victim will adjusted by shock magnitude or release of held items.

Weighted-chain reach can be set one through four yards with ready. It uses whip disarm/entangle/ready rules and flail defense penalties. Headroom and nearby obstacles determine legality before rolling.

When a weapon parries the chain, immediate chain skill success entangles it; failure has no effect, critical failure drops chain. Defender can clear using a free hand and dexterity; otherwise next-turn disarm skips hit roll but still consumes an attack.
Weighted-chain critical-miss table outcomes 3,4,17,18 become self-hit to face. Override table result after selecting weapon-specific behavior, without also breaking weapon.

Advanced cutting-filament whip length one through seven changes reach/ready time through ready action. A taut snare inflicts thrust+1d cutting with divisor ten each turn until escape; specify actual pull state and turn ownership.
A drop-weapon critical outcome for cutting-filament whip becomes self/friendly hit. Require concrete target selection and damage contract rather than an unrestricted event callback.

Authored improvised trick specifies eligibility, novelty/history, intelligence check by actor/victim or contest, and consequences. Track prior exposure so repeated trick use does not automatically retain surprise; generic permission callback is insufficient.

Harmless liquid toss has accuracy one, maximum three yards and face penalty -5. It cannot be parried. Critical hit blinds for secretly rolled 1d seconds; ordinary hit allows legal defense then will to avoid flinch.

Failed will after liquid contact gives -2 further defenses that turn and -2 dexterity/sense checks next turn. Successful will avoids flinch; relevant temperament traits and hazardous liquid effects resolve separately.

Optional malfunction applies to firearms, grenades and incendiaries only. Compare unmodified attack dice with actual malfunction threshold regardless of skill; selected weapon behavior can override generic failure-to-fire.

Fine/very-fine firearm adds one threshold, cheap subtracts one. Specific definitions and authored mistreatment/maintenance/damage can change threshold. Apply quality once and record degradation cause.

Mechanical/electrical failure prevents firing; one ready plus maintenance skill or intelligence-based weapon skill diagnoses. Each repair attempt takes one hour and maintenance check; critical failure destroys weapon. Grenade equivalent delays detonation by 1d seconds.

Misfire diagnosis uses maintenance+2 or intelligence-based weapon skill and ready. Revolver’s next shot works; other correction attempts require three ready actions, two free hands and the same check. Critical failure escalates to mechanical fault. Grenade equivalent is a permanent dud.

Stoppage fires exactly one normal shot before fault. Clearing requires three ready actions, two hands, maintenance or intelligence-based weapon skill-4; ordinary failure allows retry, critical escalates. Beam weapons become mechanical fault; single-use devices become duds. Charge only actual ammunition fired.

High malfunction outcome can explode technology-three firearms or specified technology-four grenade/breechloading/repeating types for 1d+2 crushing explosion plus 2d fragments, or actual explosive warhead damage. Technology-five-plus instead mechanical fault; resolve unlisted combinations explicitly.

Up/down effective range adjustment applies to projectiles, not beams. Downward subtract half elevation difference with floor half ground distance; upward add elevation difference. Preserve geometric ground distance and reconcile division rounding.

Seeing over cover ordinarily exposes head/neck. One-handed firing exposes weapon arm/hand; two-handed firing also exposes both arms/hands and half torso/vitals unless a firing slit permits otherwise. Actual cover height and posture determine additional exposure; complete with B408 continuation.
Technology 3 base malfunction threshold is 12; apply actual weapon overrides and quality.
Technology 4 base malfunction threshold is 14; apply actual weapon overrides and quality.
Technology 5 base malfunction threshold is 16; apply actual weapon overrides and quality.
Technology 6 and higher base malfunction threshold is 17; apply actual weapon overrides and quality.
Three-dice malfunction result 3–4 selects mechanical/electrical; dispatch by actual device category.
Three-dice malfunction result 5–8 selects misfire; dispatch by actual device category.
Three-dice malfunction result 9–11 selects stoppage; dispatch by actual device category.
Three-dice malfunction result 12–14 selects misfire; dispatch by actual device category.
Three-dice malfunction result 15–18 selects mechanical/electrical with qualifying explosion; dispatch by actual device category.
